key_insight: A tabulated-chemistry RANS model that explicitly includes preferential and differential diffusion can capture the main thermo-diffusive behavior of lean hydrogen slot flames much more faithfully than unity-Lewis or table-only corrections.
engineering_relevance: This improves the predictive reliability of low-cost CFD for hydrogen combustor design, where flame length, heat release, and extinction/instability sensitivity are strongly affected by diffusion physics.
method: Extended a tabulated-chemistry framework to RANS with transport equations for progress variable and mixture fraction.
Included mixture-averaged diffusion and Soret effect, plus a presumed-PDF turbulence–chemistry interaction model.
Benchmarked against DNS at two Reynolds numbers and compared against unity-Lewis and thermo-diffusion-only variants.
evidence_signal: Against DNS for a lean premixed H2-air slot burner at Re = 5500 and 11000, the model reproduced flame length, heat-release distribution, and the equivalence-ratio/super-adiabatic temperature branches.
watch_item: Performance still depends on the chosen turbulence closures for turbulent diffusion, scalar dissipation rate, and Reynolds stresses, so calibration and model consistency matter.
paper_title: Preferential and differential diffusion in RANS simulation of lean hydrogen flames with tabulated chemistry
